body:
## Summary

`formal-ai with codex …` passes its provider block as **global** `-c` overrides, placed *before* the
`exec` subcommand. codex-cli **0.146.0 silently discards every override given before the subcommand
as soon as the caller adds any `-c` of its own after it.** The session then resolves
`model_provider = openai`, `base_url = None`, and every request goes to `api.openai.com` and returns
`401 Unauthorized` — even though a Formal AI server is running and reachable.

This is the root cause of
[link-assistant/hive-mind#2130](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/2130)'s codex run.
Hive Mind appends `-c model_reasoning_effort=… -c model_reasoning_summary=auto` after `exec`, which
is a perfectly ordinary thing for a caller to do, and that alone is enough to lose the whole provider
configuration.

## Reproduction

Script: [`repro-codex-c-order.sh`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/main/experiments/issue-2130/repro-codex-c-order.sh)

It runs the *same* prompt three ways against a fresh `CODEX_HOME` with an identical `config.toml`,
changing **only where the `-c` overrides sit**, then reads `payload.model_provider` back out of each
session rollout:

```bash
PROVIDER=(
  -c "model_providers.formalai.name=formal-ai server"
  -c "model_providers.formalai.base_url=$BASE_URL"
  -c "model_providers.formalai.env_key=FORMAL_AI_API_KEY"
  -c "model_providers.formalai.wire_api=responses"
  -c 'model_provider=formalai'
  -c 'model=formal-ai'
)
HIVE=(-c 'model_reasoning_effort=none' -c 'model_reasoning_summary=auto')

# A — the wrapper's own layout
codex "${PROVIDER[@]}" exec --model formal-ai --json --skip-git-repo-check --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox
# B — production: the caller adds two of its own AFTER exec
codex "${PROVIDER[@]}" exec --model formal-ai --json --skip-git-repo-check "${HIVE[@]}" --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox
# C — the workaround: everything before exec
codex "${PROVIDER[@]}" "${HIVE[@]}" exec --model formal-ai --json --skip-git-repo-check --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox
```

### Result

| Variant | `-c` placement | Session `model_provider` | 401s | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A `before` | provider block only, all before `exec` | `formalai` | 0 | reaches Formal AI — `turn.completed`, `input_tokens: 24484`, exit 0 |
| B `after` | provider block before `exec` **+ caller's after** | `openai` | 7 | `401 Unauthorized` against `api.openai.com`, `turn.failed`, exit 1 |
| C `fixed` | both sets before `exec` | `formalai` | 0 | identical to A |

Variant B's stderr:

```text
ERROR codex_api::endpoint::responses_websocket: failed to connect to websocket:
  HTTP error: 401 Unauthorized, url: wss://api.openai.com/v1/responses
```

which matches the production log verbatim
(`provider=ModelProviderInfo { name: "OpenAI", base_url: None }`).

Environment: formal-ai 0.317.0, codex-cli 0.146.0, Linux, `formal-ai serve --agent-mode` on
`127.0.0.1:8123`.

## Workarounds (both verified)

1. **Place the provider overrides after `exec`** so they sit in the same group as the caller's — i.e.
   emit `codex exec <caller args> -c model_provider=formalai …` rather than
   `codex -c model_provider=formalai … exec <caller args>`.
2. **Hand codex a prepared `CODEX_HOME`** containing a `config.toml` with the provider block, and
   pass no `-c` at all. codex reads its entire configuration — provider, model catalog — from
   `CODEX_HOME`, so nothing depends on argv ordering. This is what Hive Mind now does
   (`src/formal-ai-runtime.lib.mjs`), and it is robust regardless of what the caller appends.

## Suggested fix

Option 2 is the better fix for the wrapper as well, because it removes the ordering dependency
entirely instead of trading one fragile position for another: write the provider block and model
catalog into the `CODEX_HOME` the wrapper already materialises
(`/tmp/formal-ai-codex-home-config-*/.codex/`), and stop passing `-c` on the command line. The
wrapper already creates that directory and already writes `formal-ai-model-catalog.json` into it, so
the change is to move the seven `-c` pairs into the same `config.toml` rather than to build new
machinery.

If the `-c` form is kept, then at minimum the overrides must be emitted **after** any subcommand the
caller supplied, and there should be a regression test asserting that a caller-supplied `-c` after
`exec` does not change the resolved `model_provider`.

## Related

- Downstream issue: link-assistant/hive-mind#2130
- Full analysis with all logs: [case study §3.3](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-2130/README.md)
- Possibly also worth reporting to `openai/codex`: silently discarding a previously supplied
  configuration group because a later group exists is surprising behaviour on its own. The wrapper
  should not depend on it either way.
title: `formal-ai with codex` loses its provider block when the caller adds any `-c` after `exec` — every request 401s against api.openai.com
